about: The `<content expr>` of a <send> that names a record carries the record as the pairs of its fields, each read when the send runs: `send.record` sends the record variable `shown` (an enum field crossing as the name its enum declares, an integer as its number) as `view.relayed`, which the machine reads back through the schema. `bump` changes the record, and the next send carries what it holds now. `view.shown` sends the payload it arrived with, taken whole as `_event.data`, and `agenda_list` is spelled with an underscore: the wire carries the name the document wrote. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: the record starts at the values its sets give it; nothing has been sent
a record variable crosses as the pairs of its fields
the record changes; nothing is sent
the fields are read when the send runs: the record as it is now
the payload of the event the transition is on is carried on whole
